title: TUI reordering and re-prioritizing are one step at a time

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`J` and `K` move an item one position per keystroke, so dragging something from the bottom
of a three-dozen-item queue to the top is dozens of presses. There is no move-to-top, no
move-to-position, and no way to set the priority score from the TUI once it exists — so
triage still means dropping to the CLI.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A move-to-top key puts the selected item first via `ops.move`.
2. A move-to-position prompt moves it there.
3. Setting importance/urgency from the TUI adjusts the score.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add move-to-top and move-to-position (prompting for a target), routed through `ops.move`,
and keys to bump importance/urgency once those fields land, so a queue can be triaged in
place. Pure `act` paths as usual.

**Not in this slice:** a full drag interaction; discrete jumps cover the pain.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Reordering and re-prioritizing a large queue takes a few keystrokes, not dozens.
